To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The bacteriolytically-active component in normal serum is complement, (2) the complement system in normal serum acts on bacterial cell walls to cause lysis, (3) the complement system is capable of lysing cells in the absence of specific antibody, and (4) the complement system can act on bacterial cell walls without the aid of properdin.

normal human serum lyses a rough strain of Escherichia coli in a reaction that is temperature-dependent, complement-dependent, pH- and ionic strength-dependent, and that is inhibited by the absorption of lysozyme from the serum.

the bacteriolytic action of normal human serum is dependent upon ionic strength and is temperature-dependent; that the bacteriolicidal action of serum is mediated by the complement system; and that lysozyme, in the absence of complement, does not lyse the organism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of complement in bacteriolysis, and the possible relationship of this system to other lytic mechanisms in which complement may be involved.
the complement-mediated bacteriolytic system in normal human serum.
the study of complement in relation to its role in bacteriolysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
normal human serum possesses a complement-dependent bacteriolytic factor, which is dependent on ionic conditions, temperature and pH, and which is capable of lysing certain gram-negative bacteria.
the complement system is a necessary factor in the lysis of E. coli by human serum.
normal human serum contains bacteriolytic factors in addition to complement, properdin and lysozyme which are not demonstrable by the methods of this investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
complement, in the presence of lysozyme, is capable of lysis of the cell wall of a rough E. coli.
the bacteriolytic system of normal serum is a complex one, dependent on complement, lysozyme and ionic strength.
normal human serum contains bacteriolytic factors in addition to complement, properdin and lysozyme, which are capable of lysing certain strains of E. coli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
complement may act on cell walls in a fashion similar to that of lysozyme and that the bacteriolytic action of complement on bacterial cell walls may not require the presence of specific antibody.
the bacteriolytic system is a useful tool for studying the complement system.
the bacteriolytic system is not an antibody-mediated system.
